explain.say: Which river is the mightiest? Not the longest, but the one that pours the most water into the sea every second. Look at the board. The bars show how much water each great river carries, and one is far bigger than all the rest.

explain.say: Look at the giant: the Amazon in South America. Every second it pours about 209,000 cubic metres of water into the Atlantic. A cubic metre is a box of water one metre on each side, as heavy as a small car. Can you imagine 209,000 of those every second?

explain.say: Next comes the Congo in Central Africa, at about 41,000. It crosses the Equator twice! Then the Ganges and Brahmaputra together, fed by monsoon rain and Himalayan snow. Can you see how far behind the Amazon they are?

explain.say: Now find the Nile, often called the longest river. It carries only about 3,000 cubic metres a second into Egypt, because it flows through desert, where water evaporates and is used for farms. So long does not mean big! Why do you think rain matters so much?

faq.q: Which river carries the most water?
faq.a: The Amazon, by far. It pours out about 209,000 cubic metres of water every second, more than the next six biggest rivers put together.
asks: What is the biggest river in the world?

faq.q: Is the Nile or the Amazon longer?
faq.a: The Nile, about 6,650 km, is usually listed as the longest river, and the Amazon, about 6,400 km, second. Some scientists measure the Amazon as longer, depending on where they say its source is.
asks: What is the longest river in the world?

faq.q: Why does the Amazon carry so much water?
faq.a: Its basin, the land that drains into it, is about 7 million square kilometres of rainforest near the Equator, where it rains heavily almost every day. Thousands of tributaries feed it.
asks: How big is the Amazon basin?

faq.a: Discharge is the amount of water flowing past a point in a river each second, measured in cubic metres per second. It is how geographers compare the size of rivers.
asks: How do you measure how much water a river carries?

faq.q: Why does the Nile carry so little water?
faq.a: After Khartoum the Nile flows through the Sahara, where almost no rain falls and no big tributaries join except the Atbara. The hot sun evaporates water, and farms and cities use a lot of it.
asks: Why is the Nile small at its mouth?

facts: The Amazon discharges an average of about 209,000 m³ of water per second.
The Amazon carries roughly one fifth of all river water reaching the oceans.
The Congo River crosses the Equator twice.
